# Nobel Prize in Physics — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nobel-prize-in-physics.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nobel-prize-in-physics.ttl`](../decks/nobel-prize-in-physics.ttl) · **Cards:** 119 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

Every Nobel Prize in Physics from 1901 to 2025, one card per prize year: 119 cards with the year on the front and the laureate or laureates on the back, and a short note, based on the Nobel Foundation's citation, on what the prize was for. Years with no award are left out; the deck ends with the 2025 prize, as the 2026 prize is announced on 6 October 2026, after the deck was made. From the Nobel Prize API and Wikidata, checked against NobelPrize.org. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose terms allow that: the Nobel Prize API, whose terms say the service is "free to use according to the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license", and Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0. The selection (every prize year with an award), the laureates and their order, the English and most Swedish names, the late awards and the multiple laureates come from the API, cross-checked with Wikidata; the changed Swedish names, the English spellings "Ilya" and "Nikolay", Raman's English name without "Sir" and the family links come from Wikidata, while Mott's English "Nevill F. Mott" is the API's name with "Sir" left out, and the added initials in "Alexei A. Abrikosov" and "Vitalij L. Ginzburg" from the API's own full names ("Ilya M. Frank" and "Nikolay G. Basov" combine Wikidata's spelling of the first name with the API's initial). The notes shorten the Nobel Foundation's motivations as the API gives them in English and Swedish, often closely following their wording; the API provides the motivations under CC0 too. Two sources were used for verification only and contributed nothing but confirmation of facts: NobelPrize.org's pages (copyright Nobel Prize Outreach: "You may not reproduce, distribute ... or otherwise use the Content without prior written permission"), read to confirm what the open sources give — the evidence quotes each year's one-sentence award statement from that year's summary page with the motivations elided (a short quotation to show what was checked; the same facts are CC0 from the same maker through the API, and the quotes are in the provenance report, not on the cards), but no text, selection or data field was taken, which also keeps clear of the EU sui generis database right in the site as a whole; and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0), which confirms four family relations and the late award of the 1914 prize, facts, with nothing copied. The API terms add conditions for applications: not to alter the data or mislead users — the deck changes six English and eight Swedish names (transliterations, the title "Sir", initials and an apostrophe), each documented in the method and under Quality control — and to credit the API as the data source, which the deck does. They also say applications may not use Nobel Prize Outreach's name or trademarks "in their titles or logos, or in any way that implies endorsement", and NobelPrize.org's terms list "Nobel Prize®" among the Nobel Foundation's trademarks. The deck's title, "Nobel Prize in Physics" / "Nobelpriset i fysik", uses the prize's name only to say what the deck is about (descriptive use), with no logo, medal or other Nobel graphics, and its description says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. As for the literature and peace decks, whether that satisfies the API terms' "titles" clause is a judgement for the publisher, flagged for Anton Wiklund before release and re-raised in Quality control rounds 3 and 6; it is still open and must be settled, and the decision recorded here, before the deck is released; the fallback is a title without the prize's name, such as "Physics laureates 1901–2025" / "Fysikpristagare 1901–2025".

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Prizes and selection. On 2026-10-04 the Nobel Prize API was queried for all Nobel Prizes in Physics (nobelPrizeCategory=phy, sorted by year) and for all physics laureates (see Queries). It returned 125 prize years, 1901–2025, and 229 laureates. Six years have no laureates: 1916, 1931, 1934, 1940, 1941 and 1942; the API's topMotivation and NobelPrize.org's summary page for each say "No Nobel Prize was awarded this year". They are left out. Each of the other 119 years became one card, with the year (the API's awardYear, the year the prize is for) on the front, tagged zxx as a number in no language. The 2026 prize is announced on 6 October 2026 (NobelPrize.org press release "The 2026 Nobel Prize announcements", fetched 2026-10-04), two days after the deck was made, so the deck ends with 2025.
3. Back: English. The laureates of each year in the order the API lists them, joined with ", " and " and ". The English names are the API's knownName.en, the names under which the Nobel Foundation lists the laureates, with initials and their spacing kept as given (J.J. Thomson, but "E. M. Purcell", as the API and Wikidata write it). Six names were changed, each documented under Quality control: (a) the API writes "Il´ja M. Frank", with an acute accent (´) standing for the Russian soft sign, and "Nicolay G. Basov"; the cards write "Ilya M. Frank" and "Nikolay G. Basov", combining the usual English spelling of the first name (Wikidata's English labels "Ilya Frank" and "Nikolay Basov") with the API's initial, as for the other laureates of 1958 and 1964; (b) the knighthood "Sir", which the API gives only for Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman and Nevill F. Mott, is left out (the cards write the API's name without the title; for Raman this is also his English Wikidata label, while for Mott the English form "Nevill F. Mott" is the API's name without "Sir", Wikidata's English label being "Nevill Francis Mott"), as the API leaves it out for the other knighted laureates such as J.J. Thomson, William Bragg and James Chadwick; "Lord Rayleigh", the name under which he is known as a scientist (a Wikidata alias in English and Swedish; the Swedish Wikipedia: "Som vetenskapsman är han känd som Lord Rayleigh"), is kept in both languages as a fixed name, not a title before a name; (c) "Alexei Abrikosov" is written "Alexei A. Abrikosov", with the initial of the patronymic in the API's fullName ("Alexei Alexeyevich Abrikosov"; also a Wikidata alias and NobelPrize.org's form), so that all three 2003 laureates have an initial; (d) the typographic apostrophe in "Anne L’Huillier" is written as the straight apostrophe of Wikidata's label "Anne L'Huillier" and of the deck's other names and notes ("Gerardus 't Hooft").
4. Back: Swedish. The same laureates joined with ", " and " och ". Each Swedish name is the API's Swedish name (knownName.se), which equals the English name except for Russian names, where the API gives the Swedish transliteration (Pavel A. Tjerenkov, Ilja M. Frank, Aleksandr M. Prochorov, Pjotr Kapitsa, Vitalij Ginzburg). Eight Swedish names were changed, each to a form that is a Wikidata Swedish label or alias (query 2) or the Swedish Wikipedia article title (query 3), or that adds an initial from the API's Swedish fullName: "Igor Jevgenjevitj Tamm" (full patronymic) to "Igor J. Tamm" (sv alias), so that all three 1958 laureates have an initial; "Nicolaj G. Basov" to "Nikolaj G. Basov" (sv alias and Swedish Wikipedia title; Swedish transliteration writes k); "Zhores Alferov" (the English transliteration) to "Zjores Alfjorov" (sv label and Swedish Wikipedia title); "Alexei Abrikosov" to "Alexej A. Abrikosov" (sv label and Swedish Wikipedia title); "Vitalij Ginzburg" to "Vitalij L. Ginzburg" (the initial of "Vitalij Lazarevitj Ginzburg", the API's Swedish fullName; sv alias "Vitalij L Ginzburg"), so that all three 2003 laureates have an initial; "Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman" and "Sir Nevill F. Mott" to "Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman" and "Nevill F. Mott" (sv labels and Swedish Wikipedia titles; see step 3, and Swedish writes titles before names in lower case); and "Anne L’Huillier" to "Anne L'Huillier" (sv label; see step 3). Other names that Swedish writes the same as English were kept as the API gives them, including where the Swedish Wikipedia title is a fuller or shorter variant (e.g. Wilhelm Röntgen, Paul Dirac).
5. Second source for every laureate. Wikidata was queried (query 1) for every item with P166 award received = Q38104 (Nobel Prize in Physics), with the year of its P585 point in time qualifier and the statement's rank. All 230 laureate-years in the API (229 laureates; John Bardeen twice) were matched by the Wikidata id the API itself gives (laureate.wikidata.id), and every one has Q38104 with the API's year, after one correction: the API links Pierre Agostini (2023) to Q122921025, which is now a redirect to Q57020342 (merged duplicate); the deck's checks use Q57020342. Wikidata also gives the prize, with no year, to Q629583, Sheldon Cooper, a fictional character in a television series; it is not a laureate and is ignored.
6. Third source. NobelPrize.org's summary page for each year 1901–2025 was fetched (one request per second, script fetch_summary.py) and compared with the cards: the laureates, the six years without an award and the late awards agree with the API. Its award sentence is quoted in each card's evidence with the motivations elided. NobelPrize.org is copyrighted and used for verification only.
7. Notes. Each card's backNote says in a few words what the prize was for. The notes shorten the motivation in the API (the Nobel Foundation's citation, which the API makes available under CC0 in English and Swedish; for 2021 alone the API has no Swedish motivation, so that year's Swedish note is translated from the English one); many follow its wording closely, with the leading "for" dropped and a word or two changed or left out, and the Swedish notes likewise follow the Swedish motivation where it reads naturally; where a year's laureates were cited for different work, the note names each part (e.g. 1978: "Kapitsa: low-temperature physics; Penzias and Wilson: discovering the cosmic microwave background."). Swedish technical terms were compared with the Swedish labels of the corresponding Wikidata items (query 4) and the eponymous terms written as those labels write them (Zeemaneffekten, Starkeffekten, Comptonspridning, Ramanspridning, Tjerenkovstrålning, Josephsoneffekt); the one exception is "Mössbauereffekten", whose Wikidata sv label (and Swedish Wikipedia title) is hyphenated, "Mössbauer-effekten", but which is written closed like the deck's other eponymous terms, as Q918552's sv alias "Mössbauereffekten" (a redirect on Swedish Wikipedia) writes it, as listed under the Wikidata source, in the definite form where the sentence needs it. The notes also give, from the API and confirmed by NobelPrize.org: the nine prizes awarded a year late (1914, 1917, 1918, 1921, 1924, 1925, 1928, 1932, 1943; the API's dateAwarded falls in the next year; for each but 1914 the summary page says the laureate "received his Nobel Prize one year later" or, for 1925, "their"; for 1914, whose NobelPrize.org pages do not mention it, the Swedish Wikipedia article on Max von Laue confirms it: "Nobelpriset tillkännagavs först hösten 1915"); Marie Curie's Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911; and John Bardeen's two physics prizes (1956, 1972). Four notes give a father-and-son link from Wikidata P40 child, confirmed by Wikipedia: William and Lawrence Bragg (1915, who shared the prize), J.J. Thomson (1906) and G.P. Thomson (1937), Niels Bohr (1922) and Aage Bohr (1975), Manne Siegbahn (1924) and Kai Siegbahn (1981). In Swedish the late award is "Priset tilldelades honom ett år senare" (the award decision, as in the API's dateAwarded; "dem" for 1925).
8. Machine checks. Every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build nobel-prize-in-physics) against live Wikidata: for every laureate, P166 includes Q38104; the English and Swedish name on the card is a Wikidata label or alias in that language (or the "mul" label) where Wikidata has that form; and the facts behind the notes' family links (P40) and Marie Curie's chemistry prize (P166 Q44585). The checks read only truthy property values and cannot see the P585 year qualifier, so the link between year and laureate is verified by query 1 and NobelPrize.org, not on every build. Name checks are left out where Wikidata does not have the Nobel Foundation's form (often an initialled form such as "Albert A. Michelson"); those names were confirmed against the API and NobelPrize.org's summary pages and are listed in Quality control. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node scripts/validate_sources.ts nobel-prize-in-physics).
9. Study direction. Front to back only: John Bardeen is on two cards (1956 and 1972), several backs are long lists of names, and a note on what the prize was for belongs with the year.
10. Reproduction. The cards were generated from the saved API and Wikidata responses by a script (gen_cards.py) that applies the name decisions in steps 3 and 4 and no other transformation, joins the names, takes the notes from a table written by hand (notes.py), writes each card's evidence from the saved responses and NobelPrize.org pages, and adds the Wikidata checks. The scripts and raw responses are kept in the authoring agent's scratch directory, not in the repository; the queries and URLs below are enough to fetch the same data again and the rules above to rebuild the cards. The changes made after review (Quality control rounds 1–3: names in steps 3 and 4, and five notes) were made to the dossier directly, with the Wikidata labels and Swedish Wikipedia texts behind them fetched on 2026-10-04 (queries 15 and 16).

## Selection

All 119 years from 1901 to 2025 in which the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded, one card per year, with every laureate of that year: the complete set, nothing chosen. Left out: the six years with no award (1916, 1931, 1934, 1940, 1941, 1942), since a card for them would have no laureate to learn; and the 2026 prize, which is announced on 6 October 2026, after this deck was made on 4 October 2026. The year is the prize year, not the year of the award decision: the 1921 prize, awarded to Albert Einstein in 1922, is on the card 1921. Items that Wikidata also credits with the prize but that are not laureates (a fictional character) are not on the cards. The notes say what each prize was for in a few words; the laureates' nationalities and affiliations are not given, as many laureates had several.

## Queries

**All Nobel Prizes in Physics, by year (saved as <scratch>/prizes.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in physics (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/prizes.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/nobelPrizes?nobelPrizeCategory=phy&limit=200&sort=asc&format=json"
```

**All physics laureates, with Swedish names, Wikidata ids and facts-page links (saved as <scratch>/laureates.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in physics (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/laureates.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates?nobelPrizeCategory=phy&limit=300&format=json"
```

**The API terms of use (CC0)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes and laureates in physics (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/terms.html "https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use-for-api-nobelprize-org-and-data-nobelprize-org/"
```

**How every SPARQL query below was run (runq.sh <name>, e.g. "runq.sh q1"): the query saved as a file in the scratch directory and sent to the Wikidata Query Service** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G https://query.wikidata.org/sparql --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/q1.json
```

**Query 1 (q1.rq): every holder of the Nobel Prize in Physics with the year, the statement's rank and English, Swedish and language-independent labels** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?enLabel ?svLabel ?mulLabel ?year ?rank WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q38104 ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?award pq:P585 ?date . }
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?mulLabel . FILTER(LANG(?mulLabel) = "mul") }
}
ORDER BY ?year ?enLabel
```

**Query 2 (q2.rq): the English, Swedish and "mul" labels and aliases of every holder of the prize** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?kind ?text WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q38104 .
  { ?laureate rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?laureate skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
```

**Query 3 (q3.rq): the Swedish and English Wikipedia articles of every holder of the prize** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?svwiki ?enwiki WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q38104 .
  OPTIONAL { ?svwiki schema:about ?laureate ; schema:isPartOf <https://sv.wikipedia.org/> . }
  OPTIONAL { ?enwiki schema:about ?laureate ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . }
}
```

**Query 4 (terms_sv.py): the Swedish labels, aliases and Swedish Wikipedia titles of the physics concepts named in the notes, looked up by English Wikipedia title (two requests of up to 40 titles; the script prints the URLs it fetched)** (Wikidata)

```
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&sites=enwiki&titles=Compton+scattering|Cloud+chamber|Raman+scattering|Cherenkov+radiation|Mössbauer+effect|Josephson+effect|Quantum+Hall+effect|Giant+magnetoresistance|Tau+(particle)|Higgs+boson|Bose–Einstein+condensate|Thermionic+emission|Aperture+synthesis|Scanning+tunneling+microscope|Optical+tweezers|Frequency+comb|Pauli+exclusion+principle|Zeeman+effect|Stark+effect|Muon+neutrino|Neutrino+oscillation|Asymptotic+freedom|Phase-contrast+microscopy|Bubble+chamber|Cyclotron|Wire+chamber|Charge-coupled+device|Light-emitting+diode|Ion+trap|Cosmic+microwave+background|Electroweak+interaction|Superfluidity|Graphene|Holography|Ionosphere|Wave–particle+duality|Positron|Antiproton|Nuclear+magnetic+resonance|Superconductivity&props=labels|aliases|sitelinks&sitefilter=svwiki&languages=sv|en&format=json
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&sites=enwiki&titles=Fractional+quantum+Hall+effect|Integrated+circuit|Heterojunction|Optical+fiber|Gravitational+wave|Exoplanet|Artificial+neural+network|Quantum+tunnelling|Ultrashort+pulse|Quantum+entanglement|Bell's+theorem|Spontaneous+symmetry+breaking|CP+violation|Pulsar|Liquid+crystal|Antiferromagnetism|Ferrimagnetism|Magnetohydrodynamics|Shell+model|Maser|Laser|Quantum+electrodynamics|Optical+pumping|Stellar+nucleosynthesis|BCS+theory|Thermionic+emission&props=labels|aliases|sitelinks&sitefilter=svwiki&languages=sv|en&format=json
```

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&ids=Q122921025|Q57020342&props=labels|descriptions|aliases|claims&languages=en|sv|mul&format=json"
```

**The summary page of every prize year 1901–2025 (fetch_summary.py), one request per second; script and style elements and tags stripped, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed, and the text from the second occurrence of "The Nobel Prize in Physics <year>" kept** (NobelPrize.org: the summary page of every Nobel Prize in Physics year and seven laureate pages)

```
For each year y from 1901 to 2025, one GET per second (Python urllib, User-Agent "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"):
https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/<y>/summary/
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 35 findings: 27 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 8 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (629 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

No factual or language-tag errors in the 119 cards; the cut-off at 2025 is right (physics 2026 is announced on 6 October) and round 5's fixes are in place. One release blocker and two Swedish style suggestions. The trademark-in-title question was verified as still open (the API terms, fetched 2026-10-04, still bar Nobel Prize Outreach's trademarks "in their titles or logos"); it is a publishing decision for Anton Wiklund, re-raised here and not decided by a reviewer. Both style suggestions were verified and applied: "Mössbauereffekten" is now written closed like the deck's other eponymous terms, and the 2020 Swedish note's Penrose part is a noun phrase following the Swedish motivation.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| deck | Whether the title "Nobel Prize in Physics" / "Nobelpriset i fysik" may use the prize's name under the Nobel Prize API terms (applications may not use Nobel Prize Outreach's trademarks in their titles) is still undecided; rounds 3–5 left it open for Anton Wiklund, and this is the last review before release. | Verified: the API terms (https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use-for-api-nobelprize-org-and-data-nobelprize-org/, fetched 2026-10-04) still say applications "may not use Nobel Prize Outreach’s name, logos, or other trademarks in their titles or logos, or in any way that implies endorsement". This is a legal and publishing judgement reserved for Anton Wiklund; a reviewer recording a decision on his behalf would misrepresent it, so the title is unchanged. The licensing text records the descriptive-use position, the fallback title "Physics laureates 1901–2025" / "Fysikpristagare 1901–2025" and that the question was re-raised in rounds 3 and 6; it must be settled, and the decision recorded in the licensing text, before the deck is released. | no change needed |
| 1961-hofstadter-mossbauer | The Swedish note writes "Mössbauer-effekten" with a hyphen, while the deck's other eponymous compounds are closed (Zeemaneffekten, Starkeffekten, Comptonspridning, Ramanspridning, Tjerenkovstrålning, Josephsoneffekt). | Verified (wbgetentities Q918552, fetched 2026-10-04): sv label and svwiki title "Mössbauer-effekten", sv alias "Mössbauereffekten"; both forms are in use. The note now writes "Mössbauereffekten" for consistency with the rest of the deck. The card's Wikidata evidence cites Q918552's sv label and alias, a check on its en label "Mössbauer effect" was added, and method step 7 and the Wikidata source's usedFor explain the exception to following the sv label. | fixed |
| 2020-penrose-genzel-ghez | In the Swedish note, Penrose's part is a bare att-clause ("att den allmänna relativitetsteorin förutsäger svarta hål") while Genzel and Ghez's part and the other notes use a noun phrase. | Verified against the API (nobelPrize/phy/2020, fetched 2026-10-04), whose Swedish motivation for Penrose is "för upptäckten att bildandet av svarta hål är en robust förutsägelse av den allmänna relativitetsteorin". The note now reads "Penrose: upptäckten att den allmänna relativitetsteorin förutsäger svarta hål; ...", and the card's API evidence quotes the Swedish motivations. | fixed |
